INTRODUCTION
It is a well-known fact that stress generates free radicals that may 
cause lipid peroxidation and affeact the antioxidant status of the body. The 
body has certain set mechanisms to exert scavenging action on free radicals 
that include some antioxidant enzyme systems like super oxide dismutase, 
catalase and glutathione peroxidase, glutathione-s-transferase and glutathione 
reductase which are involved in the detoxification of reactive oxygen species 
directly or indirectly Low levels of these antioxidant enzymes will cause 
accumulation of free radicals and may finally actively participate in the 
process of tissue injury (Mulden et al, 1991). According to another study 
free radicals damage tissue both at cellular and sub-cellular level by causing 
lipid peroxidation in the cell membranes and the inactivation of membrane 
bound enzymes (Florence, 1995).
India has been arranging expeditions to Antarctica for the last two 
decades. An Antarctic expeditioner has to face and cope up with many 
physical and psychological stresses apart from the stress related to UV 
radiations, magnetic field, high wind velocity, extreme cold conditions, and 
circadian biorhythms. Men living in Antarctica also suffer significant 
emotional strain as a result of physical isolation and social deprivation in 
addition to physiological stress imposed by few factors mentioned earlier 
(Roy and Dev, 1999). At the same time exposure to extreme cold poses 
stress and causes a number of metabolic disturbances in addition to problems 
of frostbite. So all these stress factors cause oxidative stress, which can be 
induced either by depletion of antioxidants and / or by an overload of oxidant 
species so that antioxidant levels become insufficient (Halliwell and 
Gutterige, 1990). In such a situation it is very important to supplement

antioxidants to keep up antioxidant status of the body. Attempts have been 
made to study the mechanisms that might be involved in man’s physiological 
responses to polar conditions. Few of them have helped in evaluating the 
nutritional requirements of men working in Polar Regions.
Ayurveda the first recorded scientific medicine in the history of the 
world emphasizes on prevention of disease and promotion of health by 
strengthening the tissue so that they can withstand the exogenous and 
endogenous stressors. This is achieved by modulating diet and life style as 
well as by the appropriate use of the phytomedicine/drugs that restore the 
equilibrium of the body (Dahanukar and Thatte, 1989a, 1989b). Over 600 
plants have been described in various Ayurvedic texts like Charak Samhita, 
Sushruta Samhita  and Nighantu.  There are interesting groups of herbs 
called rasayana  herbs that have proven adaptogenic properties. The word 
RASAYANA means the path that plasma follows {RASA- Plasma; AYANA-  
Path). It is believed that in Ayurveda the qualities of RASA DHATU (plasma  
tissue) influence the health of other dhatu’s (Tissues) of the body. Hence 
any medicine that improves the quality of RASA should strengthen or promote 
the health of all tissues of body. So these rasayana  herbs are said to prevent 
aging, re-establish youth, strengthen life and brain power and prevent disease 
all of which imply that they increase the resistance of body against any 
onslaught and act as non-specific adaptogen (Ghaniker, 1981).
Although there is a provision of very good nutritional diet to the 
members of the expedition, yet the scientific field lacks the data related to 
nutritional requirements in stressful Antarctic climate. Keeping the above 
view in mind, a food supplement of various rasayana  herbs was prepared 
and a study was carried out to look into the adaptogenic effects of rasayana  
herbs on aging process at Antarctica.
SUBJECTS AND METHODS
The study was conducted on Indian station “Maitri” on subjects out of 
the 23rd Indian Scientific Expedition to Antarctica. Out of total 50 team 
members, 21 members volunteered for supporting this study. All the members 
were briefed about the project and informed consent was taken to join the 
study as per international ethical guidelines. The trial drug was tested for 
heavy metals and it was free from cadmium, lead and arsenic. The food 
supplement was also tested for microbial load and total bacterial count was
